subject: general
question:
Fill in the blank with most appropriate option.

Trust in god _______ do the right.
solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The phrase "Trust in god" suggests a continuation towards doing something based on that trust.
 
• The correct conjunction to express this continuity without a contrast is "and".
 
• Option 2, **"and"**, naturally connects the two parts of the sentence to indicate that trusting in god should be accompanied by doing the right thing.
 
• The sentence with the blank filled would read: *"Trust in god **and** do the right."* This implies that trusting in god should be coupled with the action of doing what is right, making the two actions complementary.

Hence, the correct answer is option 2.

Correct sentence: *Trust in god **and** do the right*.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Option 1, "but"**: This conjunction is used to introduce a phrase or clause contrasting with what has already been mentioned. It is not suitable here as there is no contrast in the idea being expressed.
 
• **Option 3, "or"**: This conjunction is used to link alternatives. It is not appropriate in this context as there is no alternative action being presented.
 
• **Option 4, "yet"**: This conjunction is used to introduce a contrasting idea that follows the logic of the first part. While it could imply a contrast or a surprising outcome, it does not fit the context of this sentence, which is about doing something as a result of trust.
